narrative:

I entered an incorrect account number, inadvertently switching XXXX digits. My next payment was scheduled to be deposited on XX/XX/year>. 

I caught the mistake on the morning of XX/XX/year> and immediately contacted my XXXX department who let me know that I should contact my bank, which I did. I let the representative know all the details of the transaction as well as the context. The Bank of America representative informed me that we should give the payment time ( XXXX business days ) to reject since the name on the deposit would not match the name on the checking account. They also submitted a missing direct deposit inquiry form, which I later learned on XX/XX/year> was closed within XXXX business day. 

On XX/XX/year>, I contacted my XXXX  department again who let me know that they would enter a reversal request for the funds from the same account that they sent it to and that it could take up to XXXX business days to process. 

On the same day I received a mailed response from Bank of America saying that there wasnt an error because they never received the direct deposit I inquired about. I assumed it wouldnt be an issue because XXXX department said they had already put in motion the reversal of the original transaction. 

On XX/XX/year>, I received word from my XXXX department that Bank of America had rejected their request for a reversal due to insufficient funds in the account where funds were incorrectly deposited. I immediately called Bank of America to inquire about this. They, again, let me know that they wouldnt deposit funds into an account that didnt match my name, but offered to enter another direct deposit inquiry which would be actioned by XXXX XXXX XXXX. 

I called back on the same day with hopes of being transferred to the fraud department. By this time, I was more aware that no investigation to where these funds went had been performed and per regulation XXXX, a provisional credit could have been issued pending the investigation. I escalated twice to XXXX senior representatives. The first escalation went to a gentleman who provided conflicting information and refused to transfer me to the fraud department because this situation didnt constitute fraud in his point of view. Per Bank of Americas own website, this is exactly a situation for fraud. My funds were incorrectly deposited into another persons account who subsequently moved the funds out of Bank of Americas control. The second representative I spoke with ultimately told me that my employers bank would need to issue the claim, though she could provide no information on what type of claim, the name of the claim, if it was an internal form, where to find it, how to submit it, a turnaround time or any further detail. Furthermore, this wasnt stated on any previous interaction with Bank of America and she could provide no reason as to why. 

Following this set of events, I contacted my XXXX department who just needed to know exactly what steps they needed to follow to issue this claim. The XXXX rep called Bank of America who said that I needed to submit another direct deposit inquiry to have Bank of America investigate this, as she, the XXXX rep, could not submit a claim on my behalf. So round and round we go, with a week of me being without the funds. I talked later with another Bank of America representative who entered a direct deposit inquiry on my behalf. 

The following day on XX/XX/year>, I called in again and was offered a direct deposit inquiry yet again with a XXXX business day turnaround time. He also suggested that I contact the state attorneys office. The concern I have is genuine as XXXX not sure this would have come to light had I not discovered and tracked this all the way through. If I followed initial instructions by Bank of America, I never wouldve processed a reversal with my XXXX department and never learned that there were insufficient funds on the reversal transaction.

Subject : Complaint Against USAA FSB for Improper Denial of Fraud Claim, Reversal of Provisional Credits, and Wrongful Use of VA XXXX  Benefits To Whom It May Concern, I am filing this complaint regarding USAA Federal Savings Bank ( USAA ) for its handling of my fraud dispute, its reversal of provisional credits without proper notice, and its subsequent use of my VA XXXX benefits to cover a negative balance created by those reversals. I am a 100 % Unemployable Veteran, and these actions have caused serious financial hardship. 

Summary of Events I disputed two unauthorized or theft-by-services transactions on my USAA account in the following amounts : {$150.00} {$3900.00} USAA initially issued provisional credits for these two transactions while it conducted its investigation. On XXXX XXXX XXXX USAA reversed both provisional credits. This caused my account balance to fall to {$3900.00}. USAA then re-applied only the {$150.00} provisional credit, bringing my account balance to {$3700.00}. 

At the time of these reversals, I did not receive any advance notice. I later learned that USAA had placed letters in the secure inbox inside the USAA app. My app notifications were not enabled, and I was unaware of these messages. Only after USAA had already reversed the provisional credits and created the large negative balance did a USAA representative assist me in turning on app notifications. USAAs own recorded phone calls will confirm that I was not notified prior to the reversal of the provisional credits. 
Improper Use of VA XXXX Benefits On XXXX XXXX XXXX, my VA XXXX Compensation in the amount of {$3800.00} was deposited into my USAA account. Because USAA had previously reversed the provisional credits and driven my account to a large negative balance, USAA immediately absorbed this entire VA XXXX payment into that negative balance. After this deposit, I was left with only {$34.00} in my account. 

On XXXX XXXX XXXX USAA then allowed an insurance payment of {$200.00} to process against my account and also charged a {$29.00} overdraft fee. As a result, my account balance became {$220.00}. 

My VA XXXX benefits are federally protected. Under 38 U.S.C. 5301 ( a ), VA benefits are exempt from levy, attachment, seizure, or setoff. USAAs use of my VA XXXX compensation to cover a negative balance created by the reversal of provisional credits appears to violate this protection. 
Regulation E and Investigation Concerns USAA denied my fraud claim and justified its decision by stating that the transactions were outside the depository agreement date. This explanation is vague and does not demonstrate that the disputed transactions were authorized. Under Regulation E ( 12 CFR 1005 ), a financial institution must conduct a reasonable, good-faith investigation, provide clear written notice of its findings, and meet strict timing and notice requirements before reversing provisional credits. 

In my case, USAA reversed the provisional credits on XXXX XXXX XXXX, without providing effective prior notice. Placing letters into an in-app inbox that I was not configured to receive notifications for does not meet the spirit of Regulation E notice requirements, particularly where the reversal of those credits would drive my account deeply negative and lead to the seizure of my VA XXXX compensation. 
Requested CFPB Action I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau : 1. Investigate USAAs handling of my fraud dispute and its compliance with Regulation XXXX, including its investigation, its notice practices, and its reversal of provisional credits. 
2. Determine whether USAA improperly used my VA XXXX benefits to offset a bank-created negative balance in violation of 38 U.S.C. 5301 ( a ).

3. Require USAA to reinstate the removed provisional credits or refund the disputed amounts of {$150.00} and {$3900.00}.

4. Require USAA to return any VA XXXX funds that were improperly applied to the negative balance. 
5. Require USAA to provide a full, transparent written explanation of its findings, its procedures, and the basis for its denial of my fraud claim. 

Conclusion I am a 100 % Unemployable Veteran and rely on my VA XXXX compensation for basic living expenses. USAAs actions have caused severe financial hardship and appear to conflict with both consumer protection laws and federal protections specific to veterans benefits. 

I appreciate the Bureaus attention to this matter and request a thorough review and corrective action as appropriate.

My name is XXXX XXXX XXXX, and I am XXXX years old. I have been a loyal Navy Federal Credit Union member for many years. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received an official letter from Navy Federal ( Ref # XXXX ) stating that my debit card ending XXXX was suspended on XX/XX/XXXX and will remain suspended for a full year until XX/XX/XXXX because my debit-card history demonstrates a violation of the Debit Card Disclosure. ( See XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX ). 

This action has left me without electronic access to my own money and has placed me in an immediate financial crisis. 

What Happened I am an XXXXyear-old retiree living on a fixed income. My Social Security, pension, and retirement deposits are routed through my Navy Federal account. I have always been diligent and immediately reported every fraudulent transaction that appeared on my account.

Like millions of Americans, my personal information has been compromised in national data breaches that were completely beyond my control. I was the victim not the cause of those fraudulent events.

Despite my full cooperation with Navy Federals fraud department, the credit union has revoked my debit-card privileges for one year and has refused to provide any alternative means of reasonable access. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I spoke with a Navy Federal supervisor who suggested I could use a prepaid card instead. I explained that, at my age, I am not technologically savvy and do not understand app-based or reloadable systems. That solution still prevents me from safely retrieving or managing my funds and does not meet the needs of an elderly consumer. 

Because of this restriction, I must now travel to a branch in person simply to withdraw cash. The branch is not easily accessible, so I must pay for rides to and from the location. This is physically exhausting, financially burdensome, and unsafe. Carrying cash home each time exposes me to serious risk of theft or loss. 

It will take at least two pay cycles to transfer my pension and retirement deposits to a different institution. Until then, I am effectively locked out of my income, unable to pay bills or purchase necessities safely. 

Violations and Regulatory Concerns 1. Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA, 15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq. ) Navy Federals own Debit Card Disclosure ( 6 Liability for Failure to Complete Electronic Fund Transfers ) promises to complete authorized transfers correctly By disabling my card for a year, Navy Federal has denied me the ability to perform lawful electronic fund transfers, violating the EFTAs guarantee of consumer access to electronic payments.

2. Unfair and Abusive Practice ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 ; CFPB UDAAP Standards ) A blanket one-year debit-card suspension for a verified fraud victim causes substantial, unavoidable harm and serves no legitimate purpose. It is an unfair and abusive act, especially when applied to an XXXX consumer who acted responsibly and cooperated fully. 

XXXX. Breach of Good Faith and Fair Dealing ( 11 Ownership and Cancellation ) While Navy Federal reserves the right to revoke cards at any time, that discretion must still be exercised in good faith. Enforcing a year-long ban without review or accommodation is arbitrary, punitive, and contrary to the implied covenant of fair dealing. 

XXXX. Age-Based Disparate Impact ( Equal Credit Opportunity Act, 15 U.S.C. 1691 ) Younger members who experience fraud are routinely reissued cards after verification. Denying an XXXX senior a replacement constitutes age-based disparate treatment, intentional or not. 

XXXX. Elder Financial Exploitation and Accessibility ( CFPB Bulletin 2016-07 ) Federal guidance directs financial institutions to protect not endanger older adults. Forcing me to handle cash and rely on unfamiliar technology increases my exposure to theft, fraud, and hardship, directly contradicting CFPB elder-protection policy. 

Why Immediate Action Is Required I can not survive for two months without safe, convenient access to my income. I depend on my debit card to purchase groceries, medication, and essential items.

Navy Federals actions are unreasonable, harmful, and discriminatory. Leaving an elderly woman without a debit card for a year is indefensible and places me at serious financial and personal risk.

Requested Relief I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau require Navy Federal Credit Union to : Immediately reinstate my debit-card access or issue a new monitored, low-limit, or chip-protected card within 10 business days.

Provide a written explanation detailing the justification and policy authority for a one-year suspension.

Offer reasonable senior accommodations that do not depend on prepaid or app-based tools.

Reimburse documented transportation or service costs incurred while accessing funds during this restriction.

Conduct a policy review ensuring Navy Federals fraud-prevention measures comply with EFTA and do not unfairly impact elderly or vulnerable members.

In conclusion, This matter is urgent. Navy Federal has knowingly placed an XXXX consumer in financial jeopardy by denying access to her own funds for a year, despite clear evidence that she was the victim of data breaches and not the cause of fraud. 

I ask the CFPB to intervene immediately, enforce compliance with federal consumer-protection laws, and compel Navy Federal Credit Union to restore my debit-card access without delay. 

Thank you for your prompt attention and protection of senior consumers like me.
